name: Le Bal
watch: The partners page lists Ville de Paris as main partner. Public partners are the Education and Culture ministries (DRAC), Région Île-de-France, the Préfecture and CNAP. Mécènes include ADAGP, Alter Equity, Fondation BIC, Fondation de France, Fondation Hermès, Fondation Linklaters and Rubis Mécénat. Rubis Mécénat is the endowment fund of the Rubis group, whose energy-distribution arm sells road, aviation and marine fuels, LPG and bitumen. That makes it a current fossil-fuel funder.

name: Lincoln Center for the Performing Arts
funding: Campus Fund supporters (June 2026) in the top Leader tier: Bloomberg Philanthropies, Kenneth Griffin and Citadel, American Express, JPMorganChase, Hearst. David Koch pledged $100M in 2008 for the theater.
watch: Activists disrupted the Met Opera's Carmen on 21 November 2025, demanding Lincoln Center remove Koch names. Griffin was targeted at the Whitney, not here.

records_note: It posts Form 990 and audited statements, a named Campus Fund supporter list of June 2026, 67 directors, and archived annual reports to 2017.

name: Listasavn Føroya (National Gallery of the Faroe Islands)
watch: Excluded funder is founding. The museum's own building page lists Augustinus Fonden (a Scandinavian Tobacco Group holder) among the funders of the 1993 extension that houses the permanent collection. The other funders were Føroya Landsstýri, Tórshavnar Kommuna, Listafelag Føroya, Fossbankin, the Dronning Margrethe og Prins Henriks Fond, Beckett-Fonden, Knud Højgaards Fond and Velux Fonden. Today the museum runs on public grants.

name: London Museum
funding: City of London Corporation and Greater London Authority public funding; admission free.
watch: 3.5% pay agreement reached with Prospect in April 2026; contested pigeon logo attribution claim.

name: Louisiana Museum of Modern Art
funding: 716k visitors in 2024. Kulturstyrelsen grant DKK 36.1M (about 26%); 2024 backers include Augustinus Fonden, A.P. Møller foundations, Ny Carlsbergfondet, Realdania, Novo Nordisk Fonden and Villum Fonden.
watch: Augustinus Fonden paid for many 2024 acquisitions and DKK 2M for the 2026 Freud show. Its investment arm holds over 25% of Scandinavian Tobacco Group.

name: Louvre Abu Dhabi
watch: Kafala labour abuses documented by HRW.
why_flagged: Owned by the Abu Dhabi Department of Culture and Tourism. Abu Dhabi pays France €400M for the Louvre name and €190M for loans under the 2007 agreement.
records_note: It posts annual reports for 2018 to 2023 and names partners and patrons; the site blocked fetches, so accounts and board could not be checked.

name: Louvre
watch: Sackler name came off in July 2019, after a PAIN protest; the Louvre cites a 20-year limit. Total faced a 2017 campaign here.
why_flagged: 2025 patron lists name Deloitte, DS Automobiles, Bloomberg, CMA CGM, EDF, Stellantis, Dior and Louis Vuitton. TotalEnergies funded exhibitions for two decades; the Louvre says no direct partnership since 2018.
records_note: The Louvre posts activity reports for 2018 to 2025, a named 2025 donor list, and its 19-member board; no separate accounts page was found.

name: Lugar de la Memoria, la Tolerancia y la Inclusión Social (LUM)
funding: Peru's Ministry of Culture pays the budget (S/ 1.84M in 2023). Small grants came from the Gerda Henkel and Ford foundations and the German, Spanish and French embassies.
watch: The Culture Ministry removed director Manuel Burga in January 2025 without explanation and barred a Palestinian film in October 2026. Miraflores shut it in 2023.

name: MAC/CCB Museu de Arte Contemporânea do Centro Cultural de Belém
funding: Run by Fundação CCB, whose bodies the Culture and Finance ministers appoint. The State Budget gives about EUR 10.5M; the 2025 subsidy was unchanged. MAC/CCB had 588,643 visitors in 2024.
watch: The Culture Minister removed CCB president Francisca Carneiro Fernandes in November 2024. A petition drew 2,000+ signatures; in 2026 the State admitted no grounds.
